results.title: Your Agents Don’t Need Another Memory API. They Need a Memory Agent. | by Dr. Majid Fekri | Oct, 2026 | Medium
results.content:
Most agent memory today is a memory API. You call `add`, you call `search`, and everything between those two calls is your problem. Which memory is stale? Which two contradict each other? Which one came from a guess rather than something the user actually said, and which tool wrote it?

Memanto takes a different position. It is a memory agent: a companion that does the work of keeping your agents’ memory true, so your agents can spend their context on the task in front of them.

Full disclosure: I’m the CTO of the team that builds Memanto, and it is open source under the MIT license. I’ll try to earn your attention the honest way. Every claim below points to behavior you can check in the docs or reproduce in an afternoon, and near the end I’ll tell you where it is still young. [...] ```
pip install memantomemanto                         # one-time setup: free cloud key, or a fully local backendmemanto agent create my-projectmemanto remember "We use PostgreSQL 16 as the primary database" --type decisionmemanto recall "what database are we on?"memanto answer "What have we decided about the data stack?"
# one-time setup: free cloud key, or a fully local backend "We use PostgreSQL 16 as the primary database" type "what database are we on?" "What have we decided about the data stack?"
```

The same install gives you a Python client that runs in-process, with no server to start:

```
import timefrom memanto import Memanto import from import
``` [...] Memanto’s work comes down to five verbs:

 Curate. Every memory arrives typed, scored for confidence, and labeled with where it came from and which tool wrote it.
 Reconcile. When two memories disagree, Memanto surfaces the conflict and lets you, or a rule you wrote, decide. Nothing is quietly overwritten.
 Consolidate. On a schedule, it summarizes the day, scans for contradictions, and retires what your policy says is stale, reversibly.
 Brief. When an agent asks, it gets a grounded answer or a short sourced brief, not a pile of loosely related snippets.
 Provision. The right memories reach every tool you work in, from Claude Code and Cursor to CrewAI and a voice agent.
